english: present participle — formed from the infinitive + d
note: lachen → lachend, schlafen → schlafend, fahren → fahrend. No exceptions worth learning — it always works.

examples.de: ein weinendes Kind, ein bellender Hund
examples.en: a crying child, a barking dog

english: the laughing child — Partizip I as an ordinary adjective
note: declines exactly like any other adjective: "ein lachendes Kind", "die lachenden Kinder". Active, something happening right now.

examples.de: Die spielenden Kinder waren sehr laut.
examples.en: The playing children were very loud.

german: die gekochten Kartoffeln (Partizip II als Adjektiv)
english: the cooked potatoes — Partizip II as an ordinary adjective
note: the same Partizip II you already use in the Perfekt and Passiv, now in front of a noun with an adjective ending.

examples.de: Ein gebrauchtes Auto ist meistens günstiger.
examples.en: A used car is usually cheaper.

english: Partizip I = active/ongoing; Partizip II = passive/completed
note: "der kochende Topf" = the pot that IS boiling (active). "die gekochte Suppe" = the soup that HAS BEEN cooked (passive, done).

examples.de: Der fahrende Zug hupte; der geparkte Wagen stand still.
examples.en: The moving train honked; the parked car stood still.

english: participle-adjectives take normal adjective endings
note: same der/die/das and ein/kein/mein rules from A2: "der schlafende Hund", "ein schlafender Hund", "die schlafenden Hunde".

examples.de: Mit dem schlafenden Baby im Arm ging sie leise hinaus.
examples.en: With the sleeping baby in her arms she quietly went out.

english: extended participle construction — a whole phrase in front of the noun
note: a compressed relative clause: everything that would be in the relative clause moves in FRONT of the participle, which sits right before the noun. Very common in formal writing.

examples.de: der auf dem Tisch liegende Brief = der Brief, der auf dem Tisch liegt
examples.en: the letter lying on the table = the letter that is lying on the table

english: the fast-moving train — an extended Partizip I construction
note: "schnell" describes how it drives; the whole phrase "schnell fahrende" sits before "Zug". Unpack it left to right: article, extra info, participle, noun.

examples.de: Die gerade ankommenden Fahrgäste drängten zur Tür.
examples.en: The passengers just arriving pushed towards the door.

german: die von der Firma entwickelte Software
english: the software developed by the company — extended Partizip II (passive sense)
note: unpacks to a passive relative clause: "die Software, die von der Firma entwickelt wurde". Extremely common in news and product descriptions.

examples.de: Die letzte Woche veröffentlichten Zahlen überraschten alle.
examples.en: The figures published last week surprised everyone.

english: converting between a relative clause and an extended participle
note: reading skill first, writing skill second: given "der Mann, der dort steht", find "der dort stehende Mann" — and back again when a sentence feels too dense.

examples.de: der 1985 gebaute Bahnhof = der Bahnhof, der 1985 gebaut wurde
examples.en: the station built in 1985 = the station that was built in 1985

english: "to be done" sense — combines with a noun like an adjective
note: unpacks to "sein + zu" (Unit 2/4): "die zu lösende Aufgabe" = "die Aufgabe, die gelöst werden muss". Formal, common on forms and in instructions.

examples.de: die noch zu klärenden Fragen
examples.en: the questions still to be clarified

english: the order that has to be dealt with quickly
note: unpacks to "der Auftrag, der schnell erledigt werden muss". Same left-to-right unpacking as any extended participle.

examples.de: die bis Freitag einzureichenden Unterlagen
examples.en: the documents that have to be submitted by Friday

english: a participle used as a noun — still declines like an adjective
note: "der/die Reisende" = the traveller (literally "the one who is travelling"). Keeps adjective endings: "ein Reisender", "die Reisenden".

examples.de: Die Reisenden werden gebeten, ihre Plätze einzunehmen.
examples.en: Travellers are asked to take their seats.

english: the employee (literally "the one employed")
note: from anstellen (Partizip II). "ein Angestellter", "die Angestellten" — same adjective-ending pattern as "der Reisende".

examples.de: Als Angestellte hat sie Anspruch auf bezahlten Urlaub.
examples.en: As an employee she's entitled to paid leave.

english: the chairperson
note: from vorsitzen (Partizip I). Common in club and committee language: "der/die Vorsitzende des Vereins".

examples.de: Die neue Vorsitzende wurde einstimmig gewählt.
examples.en: The new chairperson was elected unanimously.

english: Partizip II describes the person who EXPERIENCES a feeling
note: "Ich bin begeistert" = I am (caused to be) enthusiastic — something made me feel this. Takes "von": "begeistert von der Idee".

examples.de: Die Zuschauer waren von dem Konzert begeistert.
examples.en: The audience was thrilled by the concert.

english: Partizip I / derived adjectives describe what CAUSES the feeling
note: "Das Konzert war spannend" = the concert (the cause) was exciting. Compare: "Ich war gespannt" = I (the person) was in suspense.

examples.de: Der Vortrag war interessant, aber ich war trotzdem gelangweilt.
examples.en: The talk was interesting, but I was bored all the same.

english: enthusiastic, thrilled (about)
note: Partizip II of begeistern, fully adjectival now: "begeistert sein von", "eine begeisterte Reaktion".

examples.de: Sie ist total begeistert von ihrem neuen Job.
examples.en: She's totally thrilled with her new job.

english: exciting, suspenseful
note: Partizip I of spannen, describes the source: "ein spannender Film". Compare "gespannt sein auf" = to look forward to, eager to see.

examples.de: Das Buch wird immer spannender.
examples.en: The book keeps getting more exciting.

english: surprising (the cause) vs. surprised (the person)
note: "eine überraschende Nachricht" (the news is surprising) vs. "ich bin überrascht" (I am surprised by it). The clearest minimal pair for this distinction.

examples.de: Die überraschende Absage hat alle überrascht.
examples.en: The surprising cancellation surprised everyone.

english: existing, available, on hand
note: a Partizip II that's now a pure adjective — no one says "*vorhanden werden" any more. "vorhanden sein" = to exist / be available.

examples.de: Ein Aufzug ist im Gebäude nicht vorhanden.
examples.en: There's no lift available in the building.

english: corresponding, appropriate; in accordance with
note: Partizip I of entsprechen, now also a postposed preposition + Dativ: "dem Gesetz entsprechend" = in accordance with the law.

examples.de: Bitte füllen Sie das entsprechende Formular aus.
examples.en: Please fill in the corresponding form.

english: concerning, regarding; the … in question
note: Partizip I of betreffen: "die betreffende Person" = the person in question. Also postposed: "die Frist, den Antrag betreffend".

examples.de: Bei Fragen wenden Sie sich an die betreffende Abteilung.
examples.en: For questions, contact the relevant department.

english: following
note: Partizip I of folgen: "die folgenden Punkte", "im Folgenden" = in what follows (a fixed phrase to introduce a list).

examples.de: Im Folgenden erkläre ich die wichtigsten Schritte.
examples.en: In what follows, I'll explain the most important steps.

english: known, well-known
note: Partizip II of kennen, fully adjectival: "bekannt für", "jemandem bekannt sein". "der/die Bekannte" (substantivised) = the acquaintance.

examples.de: Die Stadt ist bekannt für ihre Altstadt.
examples.en: The city is known for its old town.

english: used — recap example verb for extended-participle practice
note: Partizip II of verwenden — a good, neutral test verb for building your own extended participles: "die häufig verwendete Methode".

examples.de: Das ist die am meisten verwendete Funktion der App.
examples.en: That's the app's most frequently used feature.

english: the nominal style — where these constructions cluster
note: official texts, news, academic writing favour packing information into noun phrases (extended participles, Genitiv chains from Unit 7) over separate clauses.

examples.de: Zeitungsartikel sind oft im Nominalstil geschrieben.
examples.en: Newspaper articles are often written in the nominal style.

english: attribute — a word or phrase that modifies a noun
note: an adjective, a Genitiv phrase, and an extended participle are all types of Attribut — different ways to add detail to a noun.

examples.de: Ein Partizip kann als Attribut vor dem Nomen stehen.
examples.en: A participle can stand as an attribute before the noun.
